faq: Can you promise more subscribers or active users?
No. Results depend on your product, audience and traffic. We fix clear friction, set up tracking so you can measure the change, and tell you honestly what the numbers show.
Which analytics tool do you use?
Firebase Analytics, Mixpanel, Amplitude or PostHog, whichever you already have. If you have none, we suggest a free option and set up basic events, billed to you only if the tool charges.
Do you follow store rules for paywalls and ratings?
Yes. Apple and Google have strict rules on upgrade screens, trial wording and rating prompts. We keep prices and renewal terms clear and ask for ratings through the official prompts only.
Do I need analytics in my app already?
No. If your app has none, the Standard and Premium packages add event tracking on the steps that matter. Basic works from a walk-through of the app and your own observations.
desc:
React Native app conversion optimization turns more of your installs into people who finish sign-up and use the app. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your first-run flow, upgrade screen and key buttons, then rebuilds the weak steps with tracking so you can see where users stop.

## Why do people install an app and never come back?

Most people decide within a few taps whether an app is worth keeping. If the first screen asks for too much, the sign-up form is long or the benefit is unclear, they close the app and move on. Nothing in your store listing can rescue that moment, because the user has already installed.

Conversion in an app means the share of new users who reach the steps that matter: creating an account, finishing onboarding, using the main feature or choosing a paid plan. Each step loses some people. Finding the step that loses the most is the starting point.

## What is React Native conversion optimization?

It is the work of improving screens, wording and flow inside a React Native app so that more users complete a chosen goal. That goal could be sign-up, first action, subscription or a rating. The work combines review, small rebuilds and event tracking.

Because React Native shares one codebase, a fix made to an onboarding screen applies to iPhone and Android together. That keeps testing and upkeep simple.

## How onboarding and upgrade screens affect revenue and retention

A good first-run flow shows the benefit before it asks for effort. Users who see value early are more likely to create an account, allow notifications and return. A short sign-up form removes typing, which is the main reason people abandon on a phone.

The upgrade screen works the same way. It should say what the paid plan includes, show the price clearly and let people leave without feeling trapped. Honest wording tends to earn more trust than pressure, and store rules also require clear subscription terms. Outcomes still depend on your product and audience, so we measure instead of assuming.

## What a well-converting app flow includes

- A first screen that states what the app does in one plain sentence.
- Sign-up that asks only for what is needed, with options such as Apple or Google sign-in where suitable.
- Two to four onboarding screens that show benefits, not feature lists.
- A permission prompt for notifications that explains why, shown at the right moment.
- An upgrade screen with clear plan names, prices and terms.
- Buttons with specific labels, such as Start free trial or Save my list.
- Event tracking on every key step, from install to first action.
- A funnel view in your analytics tool, so drop-off is visible.
- A rating prompt placed after a positive moment, never on launch.

## What we do

We start with a review of your onboarding, sign-up and upgrade screens, using your analytics if you have them. We write down what slows users and which fixes are worth making first.

Then we rebuild the weak spots in your app code. Basic fixes the worst steps and shortens the form. Standard rebuilds onboarding, rewrites the upgrade screen and adds event tracking with a funnel view. Premium adds an A/B test with Firebase, a rating prompt and a well-timed notification prompt, with handover notes so your team can run the next test.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Pick one main goal for new users and design the flow around it.
- Let people try the app before asking them to register, where possible.
- Write button labels that describe the result of the tap.
- Change one thing at a time so you can see what worked.
- Show subscription terms and cancellation information clearly.

**Avoid:**
- Hiding the close button on an upgrade screen.
- Asking for a rating or notification permission on first launch.
- Counting downloads as success when few people open the app twice.
- Adding long tutorials that users cannot skip.
- Using countdown tricks that break store guidelines.

## Who this service is for

An app owner with many installs but few sign-ups. A subscription app whose upgrade screen has not changed since launch. A founder who has analytics installed but never looked at the numbers and wants someone to read the funnel with them.

## What we need from you

Repository access as a collaborator, a short note on your main goal, and screenshots of your analytics if you have any. If you have none, we can add basic tracking as part of the work. We never need passwords, and store access is only needed if you want us to help with a release.
